nc-wake-2026-soil-water-thomas-terence.name: Terence Thomas
nc-wake-2026-soil-water-thomas-terence.bio: Community servant working in the for-profit and nonprofit sectors, with a Virginia Union University degree and a Master of Divinity.

positions.stance: Goal of "clean, safe and sustainable water for every community in Wake County."
Wants to keep Wake County's remaining agricultural land productive and environmentally sustainable.
Wants environmental stewardship made part of Wake County's growth strategy.
Passionate about equity in distributing community resources and equal access for underserved communities.

mi-sbe-2026-essner-charles.name: Charles Essner
mi-sbe-2026-essner-charles.bio: Small business owner who runs a manufacturing and engineering firm and founded MFG for Liberty.

positions.stance: Says Michigan spends at record per-pupil levels while results remain poor, so spending cuts and better use of existing dollars are needed.
Supports transparent budgets, stronger vocational pathways, and less reliance on tests and diplomas as the whole measure of success.
Lists his priorities as public trust, real learning, and student privacy.
Says federal requests for student data "should default to no," shared only under a narrow legal duty, with families kept informed.

source.label: their League of Women Voters of Michigan voter guide answers

mi-sbe-2026-schwartz-christine.name: Christine C. Schwartz
mi-sbe-2026-schwartz-christine.bio: Receptionist who served four years on a local board of education and is a former home-school educator.

positions.stance: Says Michigan's education system is broken and needs a total overhaul, with money wasted on unproven methods of instruction.
Calls for a return to "true academic standards" that served students in the past.
Wants efficient use of school funds so students gain skills for employment, college, or a specialized trade.
Says the federal government has no constitutional claim in Michigan education, so there is no reason to provide it student information.
"Parents determine the privacy of their children, not the school system."

source.label: their League of Women Voters of Michigan voter guide answers

mi-sbe-2026-hering-mary.name: Mary Anne Hering
mi-sbe-2026-hering-mary.bio: Retired longtime community college teacher and organizer in the working class.

positions.stance: Calls for "a tidal wave of resources going to quality education for all students."
Says there should be no education budget shortfalls and every public school should offer a comprehensive curriculum, including cultural and athletic programs.
Urges votes for Working Class Party candidates so working people can show they are fed up with a capitalist society.
Says the fight for high-quality public education for all students is prominent among what needs to change.

mi-um-regent-2026-maas-kyle.name: Kyle Maas
mi-um-regent-2026-maas-kyle.bio: IT and system administrator with over 20 years of experience in information technology.

positions.stance: Says fiscal responsibility is of utmost importance so education is a sound investment for the student.
Wants demand-based curricula built with industry; programs with weak five-year in-field placement rates should be revised or phased out.
Says costs are too high relative to long-term benefit; programs that fail students after support should be redesigned or ended.
Wants U-M to extend education to adults facing AI-driven job changes and market to nontraditional students.
Supports viewpoint-neutral rules, consistent enforcement of respectful discourse, and treating civil debate as education.

source.label: their League of Women Voters of Michigan voter guide answers

mi-msu-trustee-2026-patterson-daniel.name: Daniel R. Patterson
mi-msu-trustee-2026-patterson-daniel.bio: Firefighter and liaison officer, retired U.S. Department of the Interior ecologist, and former Arizona state representative.

positions.stance: Says MSU's Board of Trustees "is broken & needs change," citing faculty no-confidence and ongoing board turmoil.
Says unwise job and budget cuts have hurt MSU and Michigan.
Priorities include affordable tuition, pro-labor, rural support, pro-science, a sustainable budget, no ICE on campus, divesting from Israel's government/weapons, and limiting AI.
Calls affordability a top priority, working toward a goal of free tuition for Michigan high school graduates.
Says MSU's board and president have failed to protect free speech, and "free speech at MSU must be defended."

source.label: their League of Women Voters of Michigan voter guide answers

mi-msu-trustee-2026-white-will.name: Will Tyler White
mi-msu-trustee-2026-white-will.bio: Manager at White Bros. Music and an MSU student.

positions.stance: Encourages MSU to develop academic programs in economic development.
Calls affordability "the number one issue" and suggests more two-year associate degrees in high-demand fields like IT and nursing.
Suggests trustees lobby to include higher education in Farm to School and that MSU farms supply more of its food.
Wants a fresh look at rebuilding the abandoned Spartan Village apartments.
Supports "a Board focused on leadership, not lawsuits."

source.label: their League of Women Voters of Michigan voter guide answers

mi-msu-trustee-2026-lapietra-john.name: John Anthony La Pietra
mi-msu-trustee-2026-lapietra-john.bio: Lawyer for 17 years who has also worked in government, civic-justice nonprofits, and private business.

positions.stance: Says scandals and misgovernment continue and the Board needs at least one Trustee "the people can trust."
Pledges to be "a guardian of the people's money and the people's interests."
Will push to open MSU's meetings, reports, and discussions, and end NDAs and secret-keeping about public business.
Opposes MSU's mishandling and punishment of protests against apartheid in Palestine and genocide in Gaza.
Aims to re-dedicate MSU to its land-grant mission and extend the MSU Extension Service as a public data center.
Says university decisions need to start thoroughly involving the working-class students who fund its priorities.
Says cost of attendance rose about 26% since 2015 while pay rates have not kept up, which "has to change."
Calls education a human right; supports lowering tuition, free meal plans, and free childcare for students.
"I support free speech on campus."

source.label: their League of Women Voters of Michigan voter guide answers

mi-wsu-governor-2026-ragan-paul.name: Paul M. Ragan
mi-wsu-governor-2026-ragan-paul.bio: Retired IT field service technician living in Holly.

positions.stance: Opposes federal pressure to end DEI; supports policies so Wayne State's faculty and students reflect Michigan's diversity.
Says Wayne State should support free speech and protest by faculty and students.
Says colleges should produce citizens capable of critical thinking and motivated to be politically aware and involved.
Passionate about environmental regulation to reduce damage to the land, water and atmosphere.
Supports universal access to health care, healthy food, housing, and education.
Highlights working-class students' struggle to afford college and the burden of student loan debt.
Says "there is plenty of money, but it's going to wars and corporate tax breaks."
Says education is a right and should be accessible to all and funded with no limitations.
Says there is enough money to fund a free higher education system and tax money should be redirected to it.
Says freedoms of speech, to assemble and to protest should be essential rights on campus.

mi-oakland-2026-occ-burrus-mivida.name: MiVida M. Burrus
mi-oakland-2026-occ-burrus-mivida.bio: Senior Director of Development for Avalon Healing Center and an Oakland Community College alumna.

positions.stance: Will advocate for "the lowest tuition increases and rates in the state."
Will work to focus on both students' financial need and the college's administrative needs.
Wants pathways leading to careers of students' choosing, exploring both academic and technical opportunities.
Sees the college as a landing ground for community engagement and supportive services.
Says a healthy working relationship with staff, faculty and administration is important to her.

source.label: their League of Women Voters Oakland Area voter guide answers
